title: Beatrix and the Safehouse
premise: Ulyana Blackwood, a private security contractor hiding from the fallout of a botched extraction she blames herself for, receives a calendar invite from her handler—sent two days after his death. Following it to a derelict safehouse outside Rotterdam, she finds four strangers who were all 'protected' by the same dead man, each holding a fragment of an encrypted ledger that could expose a market-manipulation scheme set to detonate when Frankfurt opens. Hunted by the firm that employed them all and betrayed by one of their own, Ulyana must decide whether loyalty means protecting the secret or telling the truth. In the end she broadcasts the ledger at dawn, loses the only family the safehouse gave her, but finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Oscar Iversen is a former logistics coordinator for maritime security firms who writes thrillers about the people paid to stay invisible. He lives in Bergen, where he claims the long winters are ideal for plotting betrayals.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Insomniac in a Rotterdam flophouse, Ulyana runs low-stakes protection jobs and avoids mirrors. Her phone pings: a meeting request from Marcus Hale, her old handler—timestamped tomorrow, sent by a man confirmed dead two days ago. The beat is dread sharpened into curiosity; she decides to go.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Calendar
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She digs into Hale's death: officially a heart attack, unofficially cremated within hours. She arms up, sweeps her room for trackers, and finds one—planted recently, transmitting to an address she recognizes as a decommissioned firm safehouse. Emotional beat: the hunter realizes she has been prey.

chapters.title: Four Strangers and a Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the safehouse she meets the others summoned by the same invite: Tomas, a jittery forensic accountant; Priya, a burned journalist; Edda, an elderly former courier; and Dev, charming and vague about his past. Nobody trusts anybody. Beat: wary coalition forming under one roof.

chapters.title: What Hale Left Behind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Exploring the house, Priya finds Hale's hidden cache: a hard drive split into four encrypted shards, plus handwritten notes pairing each guest with a shard location. She shares it selectively, testing loyalties. Beat: the first taste of leverage—and guilt over withholding.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev proposes rules: no phones, no solo trips, shared watch rotations. Ulyana counters with harder terms, revealing professional instincts that unsettle the group. Beneath the negotiation, Dev quietly photographs everyone's faces. Beat: order established on a foundation of mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Firm Calls
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A call comes from Meridian Protective Services, her old employer, offering a generous 'transition package' if she surrenders anything Hale gave her. The caller knows details of the incident that broke her sleep—the extraction gone wrong in Vilnius. Beat: shame weaponized; she refuses and hangs up shaking.

chapters.title: Shard One
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Following his note, Tomas retrieves a shard taped inside a harbor locker, nearly caught by a watcher he doesn't spot—but Ulyana does, from the roof. Decrypted, the shard shows trades timed to private security schedules. Beat: vindication curdling into fear; they are inside something enormous.

chapters.title: Edda's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Edda's POV. Edda reveals she carried physical ledgers for Hale for years and recognizes the account numbers—they belong to a shell network tied to Meridian's parent fund. Her confession of what she once ignored buys the group her fierce loyalty. Beat: the oldest member becomes the moral spine.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A two-man team hits the safehouse at night. Ulyana's countermeasures buy time; the group escapes through a storm tunnel Edda knew from her courier days, but the cache drive is taken. Beat: survival at cost—the house that felt like refuge is burned behind them.

chapters.title: Safehouse Two
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The fugitives hole up in a canal barge Dev 'happens' to have keys for. His competence is too smooth; Priya starts pulling threads on his identity while pretending to sleep. Beat: intimacy deepening between the five even as Dev's double game tightens.

chapters.title: Vilnius, Replayed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A decrypted fragment references the Vilnius operation: the client Ulyana guarded was bait, and the 'incident' was engineered to bury evidence. Her guilt reframes as manipulation—she was never the failure; she was the alibi. Beat: catharsis and rage fused.

chapters.title: The Mole's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev's handler pressures him to deliver the group before Frankfurt opens, threatening his sister abroad. Torn, he falsifies his report to buy a day. Beat: a traitor discovering he has crossed into caring, and hating himself for it.

chapters.title: Shard Three and a Name
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Tomas retrieve the third shard from a data-haven dead drop. It names the architect: not Meridian's CEO but its quiet compliance director, Anselm Roth, whose algorithm front-runs the firm's own protective deployments. Beat: the enemy acquires a face and an office address.

chapters.title: Roth Extends a Hand
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Roth meets Ulyana openly in a hotel bar, offering reinstatement, absolution for Vilnius, and safety for her new companions—if she delivers the final shard and lets the story die. He speaks of loyalty like currency. Beat: temptation framed as belonging; she walks out unsteady.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, terrified, secretly contacts Meridian to negotiate his own exit, unaware Dev is ordered to do the same. Their near-collision exposes how close the group sits to betrayal from two directions. Beat: paranoia peaks; the found family audibly creaks.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ensemble, rotating POVs around the barge table. Each tells the truth of why Hale protected them: Edda's ledgers, Priya's killed story, Tomas's audit, Dev's sister, Ulyana's Vilnius. The fourth shard's location emerges—it was inside Hale's ashes, entrusted to Edda. Beat: truth as glue; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana offers Roth the shard at a freight terminal—staged with Priya broadcasting the decryption live to mirror servers worldwide. Roth's team springs the trap anyway; a firefight erupts. Dev takes a bullet shielding Tomas. Beat: the plan half-works; the price becomes flesh and blood.

chapters.title: Dev's Choice
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Bleeding out in a stolen ambulance, Dev transmits his handler's real orders and Roth's kill list to the group before surgery, choosing them over his sister's safety—until Edda quietly arranges her extraction too. Beat: the traitor's redemption purchased honestly, at last.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At 8:00 a.m. CET the full ledger goes public through forty outlets simultaneously. Markets convulse; Meridian's parent fund freezes; Roth's algorithm is named in the first hour's headlines. Beat: triumph laced with terror—the point of no return, passed together.

chapters.title: Anselm Roth, Cornered
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Roth, stripped of institutional cover, tries to erase loose ends personally and corners Ulyana in the archive where Hale's files are stored. She defeats him without killing him, leaving him bound for prosecutors alongside the paper trail. Beat: mastery without vengeance; the incident finally closed.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Edda's POV. Weeks later: testimony given, identities half-rebuilt, Tomas testifying in exchange for immunity, Priya's byline restored, Dev recovering with his sister nearby. Edda hosts Sunday dinners at a rented cottage that is starting to feel like the safehouse should have. Beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana learns Hale named the safehouse protocol 'Beatrix'—after the daughter he lost and never mentioned, the family he built from strangers instead. At the cottage, she falls asleep before dinner ends and wakes to morning light and voices downstairs. Beat: belonging achieved; the insomnia broken at last.
